sentences.text: Eleutherornis cotei was an extinct flightless predatory bird that could reach a total height of 1.5 meters.
Specimens show a mix of primitive and advanced anatomical features.
A specific bone structure in the foot, the tarchlea of the second tarsometatarsus, is enlarged in the middle section, a trait shared with psilopterines.
Fossils were first reported from Egerkingen, Switzerland, in 1929.
The type specimen, which is the specimen the species is based on, was described by Gaillard between 1936 and 1937 from near Listeu, France, and originally named Diatryma cotei.
Schaub later named Eleutherornis helveticus in 1940 based on Swiss fossils he believed to be a ratite.
The genus Eleutherornis was formally established by Schaub in 1940, with the type species Eleutherornis cotei originally described by Gaillard in 1936.
It is classified within the order Cariamiformes, which includes modern seriemas and extinct phorusrhacids.
Eleutherornis is placed in the family Phorusrhacidae and the subfamily Psilopterinae.
This animal lived between 48.07 and 37.71 million years ago during the Lutetian to Bartonian stages.
It is debated whether Eleutherornis is a European member of the phorusrhacid family, as some researchers dispute this claim due to a lack of additional material.
Definitive phylogenetic classification of Eleutherornis is currently impossible because the known fossils are fragmentary.
In 2024, LaBarge, Garderner, and Organ questioned the identity of Eleutherornis as a phorusrhacid after excluding it from their phylogenetic analysis.
